title: Lithium Dosing Study
official: Dosing Study of Lithium Orotate for Safety, Tolerability, and Feasibility for Early Stages of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
summary: LiDS is a dosing study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and feasibility of daily oral Lithium Orotate (LiO) in aging adults at increased risk for progression of cognitive problems, including Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Age 60 years or older at study entry.

Self-reported ability to read and understand English. As all study surveys have been validated in English, we will limit participation to potential subjects able to read English.

Able to provide informed consent.

Must meet criteria for one of the three following cognitive statuses:

1. Cognitively normal/unimpaired (MoCA-22 score 19 to 22 with presence of subjective cognitive concerns and without significant hearing impairment)
2. For those without significant hearing impairment, MoCA-22 score 12 to 18 (mild objective cognitive impairment); or for those with significant hearing impairment, self-reported clinician diagnosis of MCI
3. For those without significant hearing impairment, MoCA-22 score 8 to 11 (moderate objective cognitive impairment); or for those with significant hearing impairment, self-reported clinician diagnosis of mild-stage AD dementia

Able and willing to adhere to study procedures.

Participants with moderate objective impairment or clinician diagnosis of AD dementia must have a study partner willing to participate in the study with them.

Exclusion Criteria:

Lithium-specific exclusions

* History of lithium toxicity, intolerance or hypersensitivity
* Use of any lithium formulation in the last six months
* History of diagnosed kidney disorders (e.g., chronic kidney disease, dialysis or renal transplant, acute kidney injury within past 6 months)
* Unstable thyroid disorders (e.g., medication change in the last 90 days) or history of thyroid surgery, radioactive iodine treatment or active thyroiditis in the last 90 days
* Unwilling to forego use of any non-study lithium formulation during the trial

Self-reported major psychiatric and neurological disorders

Bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or unstable major depression (e.g., recent hospitalization, medication change in the last 90 days).

To optimize participant safety and to ensure that individuals with any degree of suicidal ideation at baseline are not included in the study, the presence of any suicidal ideation at screening will be defined as a score of \>0 on PHQ-9 Item 9 or as spontaneously reported during screening.

Parkinson disease or other non-AD neurodegenerative disorders (e.g., Huntington's disease).

Self-reported medical conditions

Diagnosis of cardiovascular disease or major cardiovascular procedures in the last 6 months (e.g., cardiac conduction abnormalities, heart attack, stroke, transient ischemic attack, angina pectoris, coronary-artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, cardioversion or ablation)

Diagnosis or treatment of cancer (except non-melanoma skin cancer) in the last 6 months

Concurrent use of anti-amyloid therapies (e.g., Donanemab, Lecanemab)

History of liver disease

Other exclusions

Lab values within the abnormal range (adjusted for age and sex where relevant) for renal function, reflex thyroid tests, and liver function

MoCA-22 score 0 to 7

Score of \>50% likelihood of significant hearing impairment according to the Hearing Handicap Inventory-Screening Version (HHIE-S), among those participants without existing clinician diagnosis (for example, clinician diagnosed MCI or clinician diagnosed mild dementia) that permits cognitive status classification

Any other serious illness or condition that, in the opinion of the investigators, would preclude safe participation or completion of the study procedures

Concurrent participant in an ongoing clinical trial involving taking a study drug or supplement

Those who report "severe" for items 21-29 on the LiSERS questionnaire

UBACC (the University of California, San Diego Brief Assessment of Capacity to Consent) \< 11 indicating inability to provide informed consent. The clinical research coordinator will conduct a comprehension check of the consent form using the UBACC, which will require a perfect score of 11 out of 11 points to indicate capacity to provide informed consent.

Those with significant hearing impairment who do not report an existing clinician diagnosis of MCI or mild AD dementia, due to concern of inaccurate cognitive status classification with sole reliance on telephone-administered MoCA-22 among these persons.

Must reside in the states of Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, or Vermont and be able to have blood draws completed at a New England Quest location in those states.

Failure to complete the baseline blood collection.
